headline: Two runs back is now a genuine restart, both with real top-end range. The threshold reading is now the oldest signal on the board. Strength remains the quiet corner.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture right now is a running restart sitting on top of a very large accumulated base. The two recent runs are short, faster-paced, and carry range from bottom to top — a clear shift away from the massive slow time-on-feet block that dominated mid-August. That trail block pushed your recent four-week total to a level far above the prior stretch, so even with the current short sessions the base underneath is deep and intact, not eroding. Strength stays the weakest link: it's still isolated singles rather than a repeating slot, and the streak counter reflects that. Steps remain high even on rest days, so background load isn't the issue — the loading side of structured strength simply hasn't found a rhythm. Treat the Polar detraining flag as an artifact of the short recent sessions against a huge prior block, not a real fitness verdict.
sections.trends: Year-to-date, you're running roughly four times the distance you'd banked by this point last year, which reframes any recent quiet stretch as a dip within a much steeper long-term climb. The shape over the last several weeks is cyclical rather than linear: a huge trail-volume spike, a genuine off-stretch, and now a short-run restart. That rhythm fits a year-round hybrid model that doesn't strictly periodise — you accumulate durability in blocks, then pivot to shorter faster work. The one thing the trend can't yet show is whether this restart sustains into a repeating weekly cadence.
sections.threshold: Your threshold figure hasn't moved in nearly two months and is now the oldest metric on the board by a wide margin. That's not evidence of decline — it simply means the recent work (either very slow ultra volume or short burst-style efforts) hasn't produced the kind of sustained controlled effort that refreshes a threshold reading. The demonstrated aerobic engine from the trail block is enormous, but the specific top-of-aerobic sharpness is currently unverified. A controlled sustained tempo would tell you where you actually stand.
sections.zones: The two recent runs show a real spread — meaningful time across the middle and touches into the top end — which is a materially different session character from the flat Z1 wall of the trail block. That contrast is healthy: burst-style range after a long slow block is a sensible re-entry. What's still missing from the distribution is a deliberate, sustained middle-zone effort rather than intensity arriving in spikes with easy recovery around it. Right now the intensity is present but scattered, not structured.
sections.hr_comparison: The most recent lift didn't capture HR, so its intensity remains a blind spot, continuing a pattern where strength effort is hard to read. Where recent strength HR does exist, it sits mostly low-aerobic with occasional climbs into the middle zones — consistent with functional circuit work rather than heavy low-rep strength. On the running side the two restart sessions carry clean top-end readings, so effort trends there are readable. Nothing in the source agreement looks off.
sections.calendar: The calendar shows the signature of a block boundary: a dense cluster of trail days, a genuine gap, and now the first tentative pair of a new phase. The running streak surviving through the off-stretch tells you the habit held even when volume didn't. Strength, by contrast, shows no clustering at all — sessions land as scattered singles across weeks, which is why it reads as the least stable thread in your week.
sections.personal_bests: Your short-distance PBs were set almost exactly a year ago, in a sharpening window — and the current short, fast restart is directionally the right kind of work to eventually approach them again, though two sessions is far too early to call anything within reach. The ultra PB from the 137 km effort is well insulated by the recent trail block. For now the bests are a marker of what a focused speed phase can produce, not a near-term target.

watch_items: Watch whether a third and fourth run land this week — two confirm a restart, but weekly cadence is still unproven.
Watch for a controlled sustained tempo effort that could finally refresh the stale threshold reading.
Watch whether strength clusters into a repeating slot rather than staying isolated singles.
Watch whether the next lift captures HR, so strength intensity stops being a blind spot.
